deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this folio. The page is a printed page, numbered 380, of a German academic report set in Fraktur. Its content and dates match the necrology section of the Göttingen Königliche Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften (Nachrichten, December 1863). The archive inventory gives the previous printed page a pencil folio mark '11' and the next a '14'; no handwriting is visible on this side.

Content of the page:
(1) It ends the obituary of the chemist Eilhard Mitscherlich (died August 1863), which begins on p. 379. It mentions:
- his Lehrbuch der Chemie of 1829, praised for its original plan and for being the first work of its kind with woodcut illustrations of apparatus;
- his late geological studies of the Eifel, left in his Nachlass for one of his sons to edit;
- his return to Persian, a study of his youth, during his final illness.
(2) Jacob Grimm, to whom that day's lecture was devoted, died 20 September of that year in Berlin, in his 79th year. He was a correspondent of the Societät from 1825, an ordinary member 1830–1837, and a foreign member thereafter.
(3) The historical-philological class lost its foreign member Johann Friedrich Böhmer, first librarian of the Frankfurt city library. He died 22 October aged 68 and is praised for the Regesta of the German kings and emperors and the Urkundenbuch of Frankfurt.
(4) The page ends by announcing a third loss of the same class, continued on p. 381 (Ludwig Döderlein).

The sheet evidently survived in Riemann's 'Primzahlen' bundle as reused or enclosed paper. Its verso or adjacent leaves may carry his notes, but nothing on this page derives from Riemann. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics. The biographical dates on this page are consistent with known facts. Grimm was born 4 Jan 1785 and died 20 Sep 1863, so he was in his 79th year. Böhmer was born 22 Apr 1795 and died 22 Oct 1863, so he was 68. (On the next page, Döderlein, born 19 Dec 1791 and died 9 Nov 1863, was 71 and in his 72nd year, so '72 Jahre alt' is slightly loose. That is outside this folio.)
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed necrology from the Göttingen academy's 1863 report (Mitscherlich, Jacob Grimm, Böhmer). It contains no mathematical content and no visible hand of Riemann. It is at most physical context for how the bundle was assembled, as reused paper.

checkable.asserts: Jacob Grimm (born Jan 1785, died Sep 1863) was in his 79th year at death.
Böhmer (born Apr 1795, died Oct 1863) was 68 years old at death.
Grimm was an ordinary member in Göttingen for 7 years (1830–1837, until the Göttingen Seven dismissal).
